subject: history_social
passage: Before dawn on May 31, 1935, an earthquake destroyed most of Quetta, in what is now the Pakistani province of Balochistan, and killed tens of thousands of people in the city and the villages around it. The rebuilding that followed was governed by a building code written specifically for the site, which limited the height of structures, required that brick walls be reinforced with steel rods set into their cavities, and laid out wider streets so that collapsing buildings would not block escape. The code, later adopted elsewhere in the region, is often cited as the one ______ consequence of a catastrophe that had almost no others: a lesson purchased at a price no one would have chosen to pay.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: The code is called "a lesson" that came out of a catastrophe with "almost no other" consequences of its kind, so the blank must mean beneficial. The text details how the code protected people (reinforced walls, escape routes), and "salutary" means producing a good effect, especially one that comes out of something unpleasant.
explanation.A: Correct. "Salutary" means beneficial, often as a hard lesson, which fits a protective code that was the one good thing to come out of the earthquake.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Incidental" means happening by chance as a minor side effect. The code was written "specifically for the site" and was a deliberate response.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Negligible" means too small to matter, which contradicts calling the code a lesson and the one consequence worth noting.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Provisional" means temporary. The code was "later adopted elsewhere in the region," so it lasted and spread.
